chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Shuayb Al-Mahamili, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), when it was the night of the twenty-first and the night of the twenty-third, would engage in supplication until the night declined. So when the night declined, he prayed.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Al-Baqir do on the 21st and 23rd nights of Ramadan?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the devotional practice of Imam Al-Baqir (peace be upon him) during the odd nights of Ramadan, particularly the 21st and 23rd, which are associated with the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr). The sequence of prolonged supplication (*du'a*) followed by prayer (*salah*) until dawn reflects the Shia emphasis on combining intimate petition with formal worship during these auspicious nights. This practice underscores the spiritual significance of these nights as times for seeking divine mercy and preparation for the Imam's reappearance.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Salih Bin Abu Hammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Shuayb Al Mahamily, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Al Fuzayl Bin Yasaar who said,

‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, whenever it was a night of the 21<sup>st</sup> and a night of the 23<sup>rd</sup> (of a Month of Ramazan), used to take to the supplication until the decline of the night. So when the night declined, he<sup>asws</sup> Prayed’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Salih ibn abu Hammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali from ibn Sinan from abu Shu’ayb al-Muhamiliy from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar who has said the following: “
Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, during the twenty-first and twenty-third nights, would pray until the end of the night, then perform (the obligatory) salat (prayer).”
